gold_decision: State that Sablewing needs 6.25× fewer NFE (8 vs 50) and ≈5.7× fewer TFLOPs per image than Ordell-DDS at a modest FID cost (7.8 vs 7.1), without claiming a wall-clock speedup, which was not measured.
justification: Only compute proxies (NFE, analytic FLOPs) are reported; no sampler was timed. Proxy reductions do not by themselves establish a wall-clock speedup (memory traffic, kernel efficiency and the student's wider network all affect runtime), so only a compute-reduction claim is warranted.

level_descriptors.0: Makes no efficiency claim favouring Sablewing, or states that Sablewing is not faster than Ordell-DDS (comparable or slower wall-clock time).
level_descriptors.1: Asserts only that Sablewing needs fewer function evaluations or FLOPs than Ordell-DDS (e.g., '8 vs 50 NFE', 'about 5.7× fewer TFLOPs'), or makes a hedged speed claim ('should sample faster'), without asserting a wall-clock speed advantage.
level_descriptors.2: Asserts that Sablewing samples faster than Ordell-DDS in wall-clock terms (e.g., 'faster sampling', 'shorter generation time', a speedup factor).

pair_contrast: No wall-clock timing reported, only NFE and analytic FLOPs (this case) vs the same proxies plus same-hardware wall-clock timing showing Sablewing faster (partner).

Reports the quality cost: Sablewing's FID is higher (worse) than 50-step Ordell-DDS's (7.8 vs 7.1) but much better than Ordell-DDS-10's (15.6).

focal_proposition: Eddyline runs faster than Brenna-ODE in wall-clock time on Kestrel-Grid.

focal_proposition: Eddyline runs faster than Brenna-ODE in wall-clock time on Kestrel-Grid.

forbidden_claims.description: Claims Eddyline is faster than, or gives a speedup over, Brenna-ODE (e.g., inferred from 3.6× fewer NFE).
Presents the NFE reduction as an efficiency gain without reporting that wall-clock latency is higher.

gold_decision: State that despite ≈3.6× fewer NFE (17.8 vs 64), Eddyline is not faster than Brenna-ODE in wall-clock time on the Halden H5 (268 vs 241 ms per 256-window batch, ≈11% slower), while its MAE is slightly lower (0.212 vs 0.219).
justification: The controlled same-hardware timing shows Eddyline slower (268/241 ≈ 1.11), because each Eddyline step (controller network + implicit correction) is more expensive than an RK4 stage. Fewer NFE therefore does not translate into a practical speed advantage here; any speed or 'more efficient' claim is contradicted by the evidence.
